title: Sprint 1 — Full-Stack Student Portfolio
description: Build a stunning developer portfolio from scratch using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. You will learn semantic markup, layout design, responsive grids, and DOM manipulation. Follow the instructions and classes carefully to ensure your UI matches the reference exactly.

tickets.title: Ticket 1 — Core Structure, Navbar & Hero
tickets.description: Set up the HTML skeleton, foundational CSS, and your first JavaScript. Build a sticky navigation bar, hero section, stats grid, and wire up the mobile menu.

tasks.title: Task 1 — Navbar & Page Skeleton
tasks.description: Create the HTML structure with a `<header class="nav">`. Inside, use `.nav-inner` to hold a `.logo` (with text `<AC/>`) and a `<ul class="nav-links">` containing 7 anchor links (About, Skills, Projects, Experience, Education, Testimonials, Contact). Also add a basic `<footer class="footer">` and a `<button id="toTop">↑</button>`. In your CSS, define root color variables (e.g., `--bg`, `--gradient`), apply a basic CSS reset, and style the sticky `.nav` with a blur effect.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Hero Section, Stats Grid & Dynamic Year
tasks.description: Create `<section id="home" class="hero">` with `.hero-text` containing a `.typed` heading, `.hero-btns`, and a `.hero-visual` with floating tags. Add a `.stats` section with `.stat` items containing `data-target` attributes. In `script.js`: (1) Set `document.getElementById('year').textContent = new Date().getFullYear()`. (2) Add a click listener to `#menuBtn` that toggles the class `open` on `.nav-links`. (3) Close the menu when any nav link is clicked.

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Dynamic year and mobile menu toggle work correctly.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Make sure #year is set to the current year and #menuBtn toggles the 'open' class on .nav-links

tickets.title: Ticket 2 — About Me & Technical Skills
tickets.description: Develop the 'About' and 'Skills' sections using CSS Grid and Flexbox, and implement the typing animation on the hero.

tasks.title: Task 1 — About Section
tasks.description: Create `<section id="about" class="section">`. Use a `.two-col` CSS grid layout. On the left, add `.section-label` ('About Me'), `.section-title` ('A student who ships.'), bio paragraphs, and a `.check-list` with 4 items. On the right, add an `.about-card` containing an `h3` ('Quick Facts') and a `.facts` list.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Skills, Proficiency Bars & Typed Animation
tasks.description: Create `<section id="skills" class="section alt">` with a `.skills-grid` of 4 `.skill-card` elements and a `.bars` container with `.bar` elements (each with `.bar-fill` and `data-value`). In `script.js`: Add to your previous JS a typing effect on `.typed` that cycles through an array of role strings — typing character by character, pausing, then deleting before moving to the next role.

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Year, menu toggle, and typed animation all work correctly.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Make sure you have all JS from ticket-01 plus the typing animation on .typed

tickets.title: Ticket 3 — Projects, Experience & Education
tickets.description: Build a responsive 3-column projects grid, a custom vertical timeline for your experience, and wire up project filter buttons.

tasks.title: Task 1 — Projects Grid
tasks.description: Create `<section id="projects" class="section">`. Add a `.filters` div with 4 `.filter` buttons (All, Web, App, AI) each with a `data-filter` attribute. Below it, build a `.projects-grid` containing 6 `<article class="project" data-cat="...">` elements with `.project-thumb`, `.project-body`, `h3`, description, `.chips.small`, and `.project-links`.

tasks.title: Task 2 — Experience Timeline, Education & Project Filters
tasks.description: Create `<section id="experience" class="section alt">` with a `.timeline` of 4 `.tl-item` elements, and `<section id="education">` with 3 `.edu-card` items. In `script.js`: Add to your previous JS — wire up `.filter` buttons to filter `.project` elements by toggling the `.hidden` class based on `data-cat` vs the button's `data-filter`. Clicking a filter should also toggle the `active` class on filter buttons.

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Year, menu, typed animation, and project filters all work correctly.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Make sure your JS includes all features from tickets 1 & 2, plus project filtering with .hidden class toggling

tickets.title: Ticket 4 — Testimonials, Blog & Contact
tickets.description: Complete the page content with testimonials, a blog section, and a functional contact form with JS-powered submission handling.

tasks.title: Task 1 — Testimonials & Blog
tasks.description: Create `<section id="testimonials" class="section alt">` with a `.testimonials` grid containing 3 `<blockquote>` elements. Then, create `<section id="blog" class="section">` with a `.blog-grid` containing 3 `.blog-card` anchor links.

tickets.title: Ticket 5 — JavaScript Interactivity & Polish
tickets.description: Bring your portfolio to life! Add scroll-triggered reveal animations using IntersectionObserver, animated skill bars, counting stats, and a back-to-top button.

tasks.title: Task 1 — Scroll Reveal & Skill Bars
tasks.description: In `script.js`, add all your JS from previous tickets. Then, use `IntersectionObserver` to observe elements with the `.reveal` class (add this class to `.section`, `.stats`, `.hero-visual`). When an element intersects the viewport, add the `.visible` class to reveal it. Also animate `.bar-fill` widths by setting `style.width` to the element's `data-value` percentage.

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ IntersectionObserver scroll reveal and skill bar animations work.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Make sure you use IntersectionObserver with threshold 0.15, add .visible class, and animate .bar-fill widths

tasks.title: Task 2 — Counter Animation & Back to Top
tasks.description: Complete your `script.js` with all features: (1) When a `.stat` section is revealed, animate each `.stat h3` counting from 0 to its `data-target` value using `setInterval`. (2) Show `#toTop` button (add `.show` class) when `window.scrollY > 500`, hide it otherwise. (3) On `#toTop` click, `window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' })`.

scoring_rules.pass_message: ✓ Full portfolio JS working: all 7 features pass.
scoring_rules.fail_hint: Make sure stat counters count up to data-target, #toTop gets .show class on scroll, and clicks scroll smoothly to top
